It is a [[Hachiman shrine|Hachiman Shrine]], dedicated to the [[kami]] [[Hachiman]]. It was established c. 1190-1199. Its main festivals are held annually on April 15 and August 15 according to the lunar calendar, and on May 14. In the former [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]], it was classified as a district shrine (郷社, ''gōsha'').
